title: Choose the landing-page composition
question: Which version makes the live research process feel like the art of the page?

options.label: Evidence Orbit
options.thesis: One question gathers visible sources, then resolves into a report as you scroll.
options.viewport: A huge serif question faces an open evidence field; Normal and Deep tabs change its topology.
options.risk: The evidence field could feel abstract unless source labels and research stages stay readable.

options.label: Split Research Desk
options.thesis: A persistent question sits beside a changing research workspace.
options.viewport: Left: the question and invitation. Right: live search, source, and review panels advanced by scroll.
options.risk: Its clear split can look conventional unless the workspace has a distinctive composition and motion.

options.label: Editorial Filmstrip
options.thesis: Research unfolds as a sequence of richly typeset frames, each showing a real stage.
options.viewport: A wide first frame opens the question; the next colored frames preview search, reading, writing, and review.
options.risk: The sequence needs careful mobile pacing so the product remains clear within the first screen.
